q:
Read the passage.

By the time the ambulance reached Mercy Hospital, Elena had already called her brother twice. She had found their father on the kitchen floor that morning, awake but unable to lift his right arm. Earlier, at breakfast, he had complained that his coffee tasted strange and that his words felt "thick." Elena, a first-year nursing student, remembered a lecture from the week before about the warning signs of a stroke, and she dialed 911 before helping him sit up. Now, in the waiting room, she wished she had paid closer attention when he slurred his words at breakfast.

Place the events in the order in which they occurred, starting with the earliest.
o: Elena finds her father on the kitchen floor
Elena's father complains that his coffee tastes strange
Elena dials 911
Elena attends a lecture on the warning signs of a stroke
The ambulance reaches Mercy Hospital
w: The passage opens near the end and looks back. The lecture was "the week before." Breakfast came "earlier" than finding him on the floor. Elena dialed 911 after finding him (before helping him sit up). The ambulance's arrival at the hospital is the latest event described before the waiting-room scene.

q:
Read the passage.

The storm reached Port Allen just after midnight. While the wind tore shingles from roofs along the harbor, volunteers at the high school had already been setting up cots in the gym for two hours; they had begun at ten o'clock, right after the mayor ordered the evacuation of the low-lying east side. The power failed at 1:30 a.m., and the hospital switched to its backup generators within seconds. At dawn, the first rescue boats went out to the east side, where floodwater had reached the second step of many porches. By noon the water had begun to drop.

According to the passage, which event happened immediately before volunteers began setting up cots?
o: The power failed and the hospital started its generators.
The storm reached Port Allen just after midnight.
The wind tore shingles from roofs along the harbor.
The mayor ordered the evacuation of the east side.
w: Volunteers began at ten o'clock, "right after the mayor ordered the evacuation." The storm, the wind damage and the power failure all came later, after midnight.

n.0: The power failed at 1:30 a.m., long after the volunteers began at ten.
n.1: Order of mention trap: the storm is mentioned first but arrived after midnight, two hours after the cots were started.
n.2: The wind damage happened while the volunteers were already working, after midnight.

q:
Read the passage.

When a caller dials 911 in Harlan County, the call first rings at the county's emergency communications center, where a call-taker answers. Before asking about the emergency, the call-taker confirms the caller's location, because a dropped call is useless if no one knows where to go. The call-taker then asks what happened and types the answers into a computer system, which suggests a priority level. A dispatcher, seated at a separate console, reads the entry and radios the nearest available ambulance. While the ambulance is on its way, the call-taker stays on the line and gives the caller first-aid instructions.

Place the steps in the order in which they occur, starting with the first.
o: The call-taker confirms the caller's location
The call-taker asks what happened and enters the answers
The call-taker gives the caller first-aid instructions
The dispatcher radios the nearest available ambulance
The call rings at the emergency communications center
w: The call reaches the center and is answered; location is confirmed "before asking about the emergency"; the details are then entered; the dispatcher reads the entry and sends an ambulance; and first-aid instructions come "while the ambulance is on its way."

q:
Read the passage.

In 1928, Alexander Fleming returned from a vacation to find mold growing on one of his plates of bacteria, with a clear ring around it where the bacteria had died. He named the substance the mold produced penicillin, but he could not purify it in useful amounts. About a decade later, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain at Oxford took up the problem, and in 1940 they showed that penicillin protected infected mice. The first human patients were treated in 1941. Mass production in the United States during World War II made the drug widely available by 1944, and the three scientists shared the Nobel Prize in 1945.

Which statement about the order of events is accurate?
o: The first human patients were treated before the mouse experiments.
Florey and Chain purified penicillin before Fleming gave it a name.
Mice were protected by penicillin a year before people were treated.
The Nobel Prize was awarded before mass production of the drug began.
w: The mouse experiments were in 1940 and the first human patients were treated in 1941, one year later.

n.0: Reverses the order: mice in 1940, people in 1941.
n.1: Reverses the order: Fleming named penicillin in 1928, about a decade before Florey and Chain began their work.
n.3: Reverses the order: wartime mass production made the drug widely available by 1944, and the prize came in 1945.

q:
Read the passage.

Dr. Mae Chen is best known for the community clinic she opened in Oakland in 1998, but her path there was not direct. She had first trained as a pharmacist, graduating in 1979. After six years at a hospital pharmacy, she entered medical school in 1985, the same year her daughter was born. She completed her residency in family medicine in 1992 and spent the next six years at a rural clinic in Nevada before returning to the Bay Area. Today the Oakland clinic serves more than 9,000 patients a year.

Place the events in Dr. Chen's career in the order in which they occurred, starting with the earliest.
o: She completes her residency in family medicine
She opens the community clinic in Oakland
She graduates as a pharmacist
She works at a rural clinic in Nevada
She enters medical school
w: Pharmacy graduation (1979), medical school (1985), residency completed (1992), six years in Nevada (1992 to 1998), then the Oakland clinic (1998). The passage mentions the clinic first, but it happened last.

q:
Read the passage.

At exactly 10:00 a.m., the fire alarm sounded on the fourth floor of Lincoln Hospital. At that same moment, the automatic fire doors swung shut, and every elevator returned to the ground floor and stopped. Nurses on the unit then closed the doors to patient rooms, beginning with the rooms closest to the stairwell. Two minutes later, the charge nurse called the operator to report that the unit was secure. The all-clear sounded at 10:12, after which the elevators were returned to service and the fire doors were reopened.

According to the passage, which event happened immediately after the elevators returned to the ground floor?
o: Nurses closed the doors to patient rooms.
The charge nurse called the hospital operator.
The automatic fire doors on the unit swung shut.
The all-clear sounded at 10:12.
w: The alarm, the fire doors and the elevators all acted "at that same moment." The next event, signaled by "then," is the nurses closing patient room doors.

n.1: The call to the operator came two minutes after the nurses closed the room doors.
n.2: The fire doors closed at the same moment as the elevators returned, not after.
n.3: The all-clear came at 10:12, several events later.

q:
Read the passage and the student's list.

At Valley Medical Center, a patient who arrives at the emergency department first stops at the triage desk, where a nurse checks vital signs and assigns a priority level. Next, a registration clerk records the patient's insurance and contact information. When a treatment room opens, the patient is moved there and examined by a physician or physician assistant. Any tests ordered, such as X-rays or blood work, are done next, and the patient waits for the results. Finally, the patient is either admitted to the hospital or discharged with instructions.

Student's list: triage; treatment room and exam; tests; admission or discharge.

Which step did the student leave out?
o: Discharge instructions given to the patient
Registration of insurance and contact information
Assignment of a priority level by the triage nurse
A follow-up visit with a specialist after discharge
w: The passage lists five steps: triage, registration, treatment room and exam, tests, and admission or discharge. The student's list skips registration, which comes between triage and the treatment room.

n.0: Discharge instructions are part of the final step, which the student included.
n.2: Assigning a priority level is part of triage, which the student included.
n.3: A follow-up visit is not part of the process the passage describes.

q:
Read the passage.

Before a new vaccine reaches a pharmacy shelf, it passes through several stages. The large phase 3 trial, which can include tens of thousands of volunteers, comes after a smaller phase 2 trial has helped researchers choose the right dose. Phase 2, in turn, follows phase 1, in which a few dozen healthy adults receive the vaccine so that researchers can check its safety. None of these human trials can begin until laboratory and animal studies suggest the vaccine is promising. If phase 3 shows that the vaccine is safe and effective, the company applies to the Food and Drug Administration for a license. Even after licensing, safety monitoring continues.

Place the stages in the order in which they occur, starting with the first.
o: Continued safety monitoring after licensing
Phase 2 trial to help choose the dose
Phase 1 trial in a few dozen healthy adults
Laboratory and animal studies
Phase 3 trial with thousands of volunteers
Application to the FDA for a license
w: The passage describes the stages backward. Laboratory and animal studies come before any human trial; phase 1 comes before phase 2, which comes before phase 3; a license is sought after phase 3; monitoring continues after licensing.

q:
Read the passage.

Rosa had worked at the corner bakery for three years by the time she enrolled in night classes at the community college. She kept her weekday job until she finished her prerequisites, then switched to weekend shifts when her clinical rotations began. Those two years were the hardest of her life. She passed her licensing exam the summer after graduation and started at County General that fall, but she still stops by the bakery every Saturday for a cinnamon roll.

According to the passage, which event happened immediately after Rosa finished her prerequisites?
o: She passed her nursing licensing exam.
She started working at County General.
She enrolled in night classes at the college.
She switched to weekend shifts at the bakery.
w: Rosa kept her weekday job "until she finished her prerequisites, then switched to weekend shifts" when clinical rotations began. The signal word "then" marks the next event.

n.0: The licensing exam came the summer after graduation, well after the switch to weekends.
n.1: She started at County General in the fall after passing her exam, the last event.
n.2: She enrolled in night classes before taking her prerequisites.

q:
Read the news brief.

The Fairmont City Council approved a new bike-share program on Tuesday, two weeks after a public hearing at which more than sixty residents spoke. The hearing itself had been scheduled after a petition with 4,000 signatures reached the mayor's office in March. Under the plan, bikes will appear at 40 stations by June, following a month-long test with city employees in May. Riders will pay $1 to unlock a bike and 15 cents per minute.

According to the news brief, which of these events happened first?
o: The city council approved the bike-share program.
A petition with 4,000 signatures reached the mayor.
More than sixty residents spoke at a public hearing.
City employees began testing the bikes in May.
w: The hearing was scheduled after the petition arrived in March, and the council vote came two weeks after the hearing. The employee test is planned for later. So the petition came first, even though it is mentioned after the vote.

n.0: Order of mention trap: the vote is mentioned first but came two weeks after the hearing.
n.2: The hearing was scheduled after the petition reached the mayor.
n.3: The May test is a future step, after the council's approval.

q:
Read the passage.

The night before her TEAS exam, Aaliyah laid out her ID and admission ticket by the front door. She woke at six, an hour before her alarm, and reviewed her flashcards over breakfast. On the drive to the testing center, she realized she had left her ID by the door and turned back for it, arriving with ten minutes to spare. The Reading section felt fast; she finished it just as the timer ran out. During the break after the Math section, she ate a granola bar and texted her mother that the hardest part was over.

Which statement about the order of events is accurate?
o: Aaliyah texted her mother before she finished the Reading section.
Aaliyah laid out her ID after she woke on the morning of the exam.
Aaliyah reviewed her flashcards after she turned back for her ID.
Aaliyah finished the Math section before she texted her mother.
w: She texted her mother during the break, and the break came after the Math section. So the Math section was finished before the text.

n.0: Reversed: the text came during the break after Math, which followed the Reading section.
n.1: Reversed: she laid out her ID the night before the exam.
n.2: Reversed: she reviewed flashcards at breakfast, before the drive on which she turned back.

q:
Read the passage and the volunteer's list.

When a new book arrives at the Hillside Library, a technician first checks it against the order list to confirm it is the right title and edition. The book is then entered into the catalog, which assigns it a call number. Next, a label with the call number is attached to the spine, and a barcode is placed inside the front cover. The book is covered with a clear plastic jacket and stamped with the library's name. Finally, it is placed on the New Arrivals cart and shelved within two days.

Volunteer's list: (1) check against the order list; (2) enter into the catalog; (3) attach the spine label and barcode; (4) check out to the patron who requested it; (5) cover with a plastic jacket and stamp.

Which step in the volunteer's list is NOT part of the process described?
o: Step 3
Step 2
Step 4
Step 5
w: Checking a book out to a patron belongs to a different process (circulation). The passage's process ends with the book on the New Arrivals cart and shelved.

n.0: Attaching the spine label and barcode is the third step in the passage.
n.1: Entering the book into the catalog is the second step in the passage.
n.3: Covering and stamping the book is the fourth step in the passage.

q: Read the paragraph from a nursing program newsletter. Select the sentence that states the main idea of the paragraph.

parts.t: Last spring, a nursing student at Lakeview College fainted during an early clinical shift.
A review later found that she had skipped breakfast and slept only four hours the night before.
When the college surveyed its nursing students, nearly half said they often missed a meal before early shifts.
For nursing students, basic self-care is not a private matter, because it affects their safety and performance on clinical units.
The program now opens a breakfast cart at 6 a.m. and includes a session on sleep in its first-year orientation.

sn.a: Last spring, a nursing student at Lakeview College fainted during an early clinical shift.
sn.b: A review later found that she had skipped breakfast and slept only four hours the night before.
sn.c: When the college surveyed its nursing students, nearly half said they often missed a meal before early shifts.
sn.d: For nursing students, basic self-care is not a private matter, because it affects their safety and performance on clinical units.
sn.e: The program now opens a breakfast cart at 6 a.m. and includes a session on sleep in its first-year orientation.

w: Sentence 4 states the general point the rest of the paragraph builds toward: students' basic self-care affects their safety and performance on clinical units. The fainting episode, its causes and the survey are evidence for that point, and the breakfast cart and sleep session are the program's response to it.

n.a: The fainting episode is an opening anecdote that draws the reader in. It is one example, not the point the paragraph makes.
n.b: This explains why one student fainted. It supports the main idea but is too narrow to be it.
n.c: The survey result shows the problem is widespread. It is supporting evidence, not the conclusion the paragraph draws from that evidence.
n.e: The breakfast cart and sleep session are actions the program took in response to the main idea. They are specific details that follow from it, not the general point itself.

q: Read the passage. Select the sentence that best supports the claim made in the first sentence.

parts.t: Over the past two decades, the school nurse's job has shifted from treating playground injuries to managing students' ongoing health needs.
At Ridgeway Middle School, nurse Dana Price spends most mornings updating care plans with the families of students who have diabetes, asthma, or seizure disorders.
Each fall, she also checks every student's vision and hearing, a screening that school nurses have done for generations.
Scraped knees and bumped heads still arrive at her door, especially after recess.
Price says the hardest part of her job is keeping up with the paperwork that new state rules require.

sn.a: Over the past two decades, the school nurse's job has shifted from treating playground injuries to managing students' ongoing health needs.
sn.b: At Ridgeway Middle School, nurse Dana Price spends most mornings updating care plans with the families of students who have diabetes, asthma, or seizure disorders.
sn.c: Each fall, she also checks every student's vision and hearing, a screening that school nurses have done for generations.
sn.d: Scraped knees and bumped heads still arrive at her door, especially after recess.
sn.e: Price says the hardest part of her job is keeping up with the paperwork that new state rules require.

w: The claim is that the job now centers on managing ongoing health needs. Updating care plans for diabetes, asthma and seizure disorders is specific evidence of exactly that kind of ongoing management, so sentence 2 supports the claim most directly.

n.a: This is the claim itself. A sentence cannot serve as support for its own statement.
n.c: Vision and hearing screening goes beyond treating injuries, but the sentence itself says school nurses have done it for generations. It shows continuity in the job, not the shift toward managing ongoing health needs.
n.d: Scraped knees are the older kind of work the claim says the job has moved away from, so this detail does not support the shift.
n.e: This reports a complaint about paperwork. It does not show any change toward managing students' ongoing health needs.

q: Read the passage. Select the sentence that best supports the inference that Marisol hides her uncertainty about the new medicine from the technician.

parts.t: Marisol reached the pharmacy counter ten minutes before closing.
She set three prescription bottles on the counter and lined them up by size.
The technician explained that her new tablet should be taken with food, and Marisol nodded quickly.
When he asked whether she had any questions, she said she was fine, but she kept turning the new bottle so that its label faced her.
Outside, she sat in her car and read the leaflet from start to finish before starting the engine.

sn.a: Marisol reached the pharmacy counter ten minutes before closing.
sn.b: She set three prescription bottles on the counter and lined them up by size.
sn.c: The technician explained that her new tablet should be taken with food, and Marisol nodded quickly.
sn.d: When he asked whether she had any questions, she said she was fine, but she kept turning the new bottle so that its label faced her.
sn.e: Outside, she sat in her car and read the leaflet from start to finish before starting the engine.

w: The inference has two parts: Marisol is unsure, and she keeps that from the technician. Sentence 4 shows both at once. She tells him she is fine, yet in front of him she keeps turning the bottle to reread its label.

n.a: Arriving just before closing may suggest she is rushed, but it says nothing about doubts over the medicine or about what she shows the technician.
n.b: Lining up the bottles suggests she is organized. It reveals neither uncertainty nor a gap between what she says and what she feels.
n.c: A quick nod signals understanding or agreement. On its own it fits a person who really did understand, so it does not show hidden uncertainty.
n.e: Reading the whole leaflet suggests she wanted more information, but it happens after she has left the counter, so it does not show her hiding anything from the technician.

q: Jordan arrives at the clinic without his appointment letter. When the kiosk displays his details, he sees that his address is out of date. Following the directions, select the one step Jordan does not complete.

parts: Self check-in at the clinic kiosk

parts.t: 1. Touch the screen to begin.
2. Scan the barcode on your appointment letter.
3. If you do not have your letter, type your date of birth instead.
4. Check that the name and address shown are correct.
5. If any detail is wrong, select "Update," correct it, and continue.
6. Take your printed ticket and wait for your number to be called.

sn.b: 2. Scan the barcode on your appointment letter.
sn.c: 3. If you do not have your letter, type your date of birth instead.
sn.d: 4. Check that the name and address shown are correct.
sn.e: 5. If any detail is wrong, select "Update," correct it, and continue.
sn.f: 6. Take your printed ticket and wait for your number to be called.

w: Step 2 needs the barcode on the appointment letter, and Jordan has no letter, so he skips it and uses step 3 instead. Every other step applies to him: he starts the kiosk, types his birth date, checks his details, updates the wrong address and takes a ticket.

n.a: Every user starts by touching the screen. Step 1 has no condition attached.
n.c: Step 3 is the alternative for people without a letter, which is exactly Jordan's situation, so he completes it.
n.d: Jordan must check his details. That is how he discovers that his address is out of date.
n.e: Step 5 applies when a detail is wrong. Jordan's address is wrong, so he selects Update and corrects it.
n.f: Step 5 says to correct the detail and continue, so Jordan still finishes by taking a ticket.

q: Read the passage. Select the sentence that describes the earliest event in the story.

parts.t: By the time the ambulance reached Mercy Hospital, Tomas had already called his sister.
He had found his grandfather on the kitchen floor that afternoon, a few minutes after returning from the hardware store.
Earlier that day, his grandfather had complained of feeling dizzy but had insisted that Tomas run the errand anyway.
Before calling his sister, Tomas had dialed 911 and followed the dispatcher's instructions to keep his grandfather still.
Now, sitting in the waiting room, Tomas wished he had stayed home.

sn.a: By the time the ambulance reached Mercy Hospital, Tomas had already called his sister.
sn.b: He had found his grandfather on the kitchen floor that afternoon, a few minutes after returning from the hardware store.
sn.c: Earlier that day, his grandfather had complained of feeling dizzy but had insisted that Tomas run the errand anyway.
sn.d: Before calling his sister, Tomas had dialed 911 and followed the dispatcher's instructions to keep his grandfather still.
sn.e: Now, sitting in the waiting room, Tomas wished he had stayed home.

w: In time order: the grandfather complains of dizziness and sends Tomas on the errand (sentence 3); Tomas returns and finds him (sentence 2); he calls 911 (sentence 4); he calls his sister (sentence 1); and he waits at the hospital (sentence 5). "Earlier that day" and the fact that the complaint came before the errand place sentence 3 first.

n.a: This is mentioned first, but the ambulance's arrival comes near the end of the events. Order of mention is not order of occurrence.
n.b: Finding his grandfather happened after Tomas returned from the errand, and the errand came after the dizziness complaint.
n.d: The 911 call came after Tomas found his grandfather, which was after the complaint earlier that day.
n.e: The waiting room is the story's present moment, the latest event described.

q: Kayla takes this medicine in the evening, as her doctor advised. At 9 p.m. she realizes she has not taken tonight's tablet. Select the sentence from the leaflet that tells her what to do.

parts.t: Take one tablet each morning with a full glass of water.
If you miss a morning dose, take it as soon as you remember that same day.
If you do not remember until the next morning, skip the missed tablet and take only your usual dose.
Do not take two tablets at once to make up for a missed dose.
If your doctor has told you to take this medicine in the evening, you may take a missed evening dose up until bedtime that night.
